name: Pushing robustness to the limits
gist: These papers build AI systems that keep working correctly even when faced with adversarial attacks, distributional shifts, or unusual inputs that weren't in training.
explain: A model trained to classify images looks at millions of pictures and learns patterns. It works great on the test set. But then you deploy it, and the real world has slightly different lighting, new objects, unusual angles. The model's performance drops. Or you have a text model trained on news articles, and you ask it to summarize scientific papers written in a different style. This is distribution shift—the test data comes from a different statistical distribution than the training data, and the model wasn't prepared for it. An even worse case is an adversarial attack: someone deliberately modifies an image by a tiny amount—invisible to humans—that causes the model to misclassify it. Or someone adds imperceptible noise to audio that changes speech recognition. These attacks show that models are brittle in surprising ways.

Why is this hard? Because models learn surface patterns, not deep understanding. A vision model might learn that 'curved white things near the top of the image means swan,' and it will see swans everywhere if you give it images with that pattern, even if it's a plastic toy. A language model trained on clean English text might struggle when faced with typos, slang, or writing from a different region. And defending against adversarial attacks seems almost paradoxical: the network can make tiny changes that flip predictions, but those changes are invisible to humans. The model has learned features that humans didn't use, and those features are fragile. Making a model resistant to one kind of attack often makes it vulnerable to another, because the model learns to use different features to compensate, and those new features might have their own vulnerabilities. There's a fundamental tension between accuracy on clean data and resistance to perturbations, because techniques that help ignore irrelevant small changes often also ignore real differences in the input that should lead to different predictions.

Researchers approach this on several fronts. One is adversarial training: teach the model to resist adversarial examples by training on them, so it learns to ignore irrelevant small changes. Another is certified defenses: prove mathematically that a model will work correctly within a certain range, using verification techniques that give guarantees rather than just hoping it works. Others study why models are brittle in the first place, trying to understand whether brittleness is an intrinsic limitation—something unavoidable because of how neural networks learn by fitting data—or something that can be overcome with better training techniques. Still others look at distribution shift directly: train on multiple domains at once, which forces the model to find general patterns that work across all of them rather than memorizing one domain's specific quirks, since features that only work on one dataset won't transfer. Some papers also study detection: can you recognize when the model is seeing out-of-distribution inputs and fall back to a safer strategy that admits uncertainty rather than guessing? The fundamental goal is to make models that work in the messy real world, not just on tidy test sets, because deployment conditions are always different from training and the model will encounter surprises.

papers.title: AdPO: Enhancing the Adversarial Robustness of Large Vision-Language Models with Preference Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 23% accuracy gains on MME, POPE, RePOPE, CHAIR with training-efficient transfer from smaller to larger LVLMs, delivering state-of-the-art performance in both clean and adversarial settings.

papers.title: Aligner, Diagnose Thyself: A Meta-Learning Paradigm for Fusing Intrinsic Feedback in Preference Alignment
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art across various noise conditions; provides first quantitative analysis showing fusion of diagnostics essential vs. any single heuristic.

papers.title: Auditing Black-Box LLM APIs with a Rank-Based Uniformity Test
papers.contribution: Accurate detection of LLM substitutions and harmful fine-tuning across diverse query domains with superior performance under constrained query budgets.

papers.title: CERTIFIED VS. EMPIRICAL ADVERSARIAL ROBUSTNESS VIA HYBRID CONVOLUTIONS WITH ATTENTION STOCHASTICITY
papers.contribution: HyCAS boosts certified accuracy by up to 7.3% and empirical robustness by up to 3.1% while maintaining clean accuracy across imaging benchmarks.

papers.title: Dual Randomized Smoothing: Beyond Global Noise Variance
papers.contribution: Achieve strong performance at both small and large radii unattainable with global variance, with 60% inference overhead.

papers.title: Dual-Space Smoothness for Robust and Balanced LLM Unlearning
papers.contribution: Outperforms SOTA baselines under multiple attacks while achieving better balance among metrics on conversational and continuous-text settings.

papers.title: Fingerprinting Deep Neural Networks for Ownership Protection: An Analytical Approach
papers.contribution: Establish theoretical bounds defining an admissible interval for stretch factor and enable practical fingerprint generation with surrogate model pools.

papers.title: Get RICH or Die Scaling: Profitably Trading Inference Compute for Robustness
papers.contribution: Empirically supports RICH across vision-language models, finding robustness gains from test-time compute correlate with base model robustness.

papers.title: Safety Mirage: How Spurious Correlations Undermine VLM Safety Fine-Tuning and Can Be Mitigated by Machine Unlearning
papers.contribution: Reduces attack success rate by up to 60.27% and cuts unnecessary rejections by over 84.20% compared to supervised fine-tuning approaches.

papers.title: TriQDef: Disrupting Semantic and Gradient Alignment to Prevent Adversarial Patch Transferability in Quantized Neural Networks
papers.contribution: TriQDef lowers Attack Success Rates by over 40% on unseen patch and quantization combinations while preserving clean accuracy.

papers.title: Understanding Sensitivity of Differential Attention through the Lens of Adversarial Robustness
papers.contribution: These results demonstrate higher attack success rates, frequent gradient opposition, and stronger local sensitivity compared to standard attention.

papers.title: A Coin Flip for Safety: LLM Judges Fail to Reliably Measure Adversarial Robustness
papers.contribution: Shows that many attacks inflate success rates by exploiting judge insufficiencies rather than eliciting genuinely harmful content; provides benchmark of more consistently judgeable behaviors.

papers.title: A-MemGuard: A Proactive Defense Framework For LLM-Based Agent Memory
papers.contribution: Effectively cuts attack success rates by over 95% while incurring minimal computational overhead.

papers.title: A2D: Any-Order, Any-Step Safety Alignment for Diffusion Language Models
papers.contribution: A2D slashes DIJA attack success rates from over 80% to near-zero (0-1.3% depending on model) while enabling real-time monitoring and early rejection.

papers.title: AEGIS: Adversarial Target–Guided Retention-Data-Free Robust Concept Erasure from Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: AEGIS simultaneously improves robustness against adversarial prompt attacks and retains model utility, hardening diffusion models against state-of-the-art attacks.

papers.title: Adversarial Attacks Already Tell the Answer: Directional Bias-Guided Test-time Defense for Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: DBD achieves state-of-the-art adversarial robustness while preserving clean accuracy; shows adversarial accuracy can surpass clean accuracy.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness of Implicit Neural Representation-Based Classifiers
papers.contribution: Shows INR-based classifiers are vulnerable with accuracy collapsing to near zero under perturbations, and existing countermeasures for discrete representations offer limited protection.

papers.title: Antibody: Strengthening Defense Against Harmful Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models via Attenuating Harmful Gradient Influence
papers.contribution: Antibody successfully mitigates harmful fine-tuning attacks while maintaining fine-tuning performance on benign user-submitted datasets.

papers.title: Bradley-Terry and Multi-Objective Reward Modeling Are Complementary
papers.contribution: The framework addresses reward hacking in out-of-distribution scenarios by leveraging complementary benefits of BT loss and regression objectives, establishing theoretical connection between the two formulations.

papers.title: Broadening the Backdoor Basin: Understanding LLM Backdoors Collapse and Making Backdoors Persistent
papers.contribution: Consistently preserves high attack success rate across multiple LLMs and SFT scenarios while maintaining competitive utility.

papers.title: CORE: Conflict-Oriented Reasoning for General Multimodal Manipulation Detection
papers.contribution: CORE surpasses state-of-the-art models by 9.7%, 14.1%, and 11.8% accuracy on DGM4, MMFakeBench, and MDSM benchmarks, generalizing to unseen manipulation types.

papers.title: CREDIT: Certified Ownership Verification of Deep Neural Networks Against Model Extraction Attacks
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art certified ownership verification against model extraction attacks across multiple datasets and domains.

papers.title: Calibrating Uncertainty for Zero-Shot Adversarial CLIP
papers.contribution: The method significantly improves uncertainty calibration and achieves competitive adversarial robustness while preserving clean accuracy across multiple zero-shot benchmarks.

papers.title: Certified Robustness under Heterogeneous Perturbations via Hybrid Randomized Smoothing
papers.contribution: Yields closed-form one-dimensional certificate strictly generalizing both Gaussian and discrete randomized smoothing, provides first model-agnostic certificate for joint discrete-token and continuous-image perturbations.

papers.title: Certifying Graph Neural Networks Against Label and Structure Poisoning
papers.contribution: Architecture-agnostic framework significantly improves robustness guarantees against node-label and graph-structure poisoning while maintaining clean accuracy on benchmarks.

papers.title: Certifying the Full YOLO Pipeline: A Probabilistic Verification Approach
papers.contribution: The method scales to practical YOLO models providing probabilistic guarantees and tighter IoU lower bounds with significantly fewer samples than existing methods.

papers.title: Class-Conditional Distribution Balancing for Group Robust Classification
papers.contribution: Delivers competitive robustness to bias-supervised methods while eliminating need for bias annotations or predictions.

papers.title: Concept Concentration for Faithful Representation Intervention
papers.contribution: Significantly reduces both in-distribution and OOD jailbreak success rates while maintaining strong performance on math and code generation.

papers.title: Contrastive Spectral Rectification: Test-Time Defense towards Zero-shot Adversarial Robustness of CLIP
papers.contribution: CSR outperforms SOTA by an average of 18.1% against strong APGD with modest overhead and exhibits broad applicability across diverse visual tasks.

papers.title: Coupled Trigger Optimization and Vulnerable Parameter Alignment for Persistent Backdoor Attacks on Federated Learning
papers.contribution: CTO-VPA achieves substantially improved backdoor persistence and robustness compared to prior attacks across multiple datasets and defense settings.

papers.title: Coverage ≠ Exposure: Auditable Control of Same-Support Tail Failures under Multimodal Missingness
papers.contribution: H-CES improves same-support tail reliability while preserving clean performance across multimodal settings.

papers.title: DARC: Disagreement-Aware Alignment via Risk-Constrained Decoding
papers.contribution: Reduces disagreement and tail risk while maintaining competitive average quality under noisy heterogeneous feedback across alignment benchmarks.

papers.title: DRIFT: Divergent Response in Filtered Transformations for Robust Adversarial Defense
papers.contribution: DRIFT achieves substantial robustness gains on ImageNet across CNNs and ViTs, outperforming preprocessing and adversarial training with negligible runtime/memory cost.

papers.title: Does a Hybrid Space-Aware Randomized Defense Improve Empirical and Certified Adversarial Robustness?
papers.contribution: Improves certified robustness by up to 9.6% and empirical robustness by up to 5% without reducing clean accuracy across diverse imaging datasets.

papers.title: Downgrade to Upgrade: Optimizer Simplification Enhances Robustness in LLM Unlearning
papers.contribution: Shows zeroth-order methods converge to harder-to-disturb loss landscape basins, with theoretical connection to randomized smoothing.

papers.title: Echoes within the Reasoning: Stealthy and Effective Watermarking via Chain of Thought
papers.contribution: BiCoT preserves reasoning fidelity across diverse reasoning tasks while achieving robust detection under fine-tuning, quantization, and adaptive attacks across in-domain and out-of-distribution settings.

papers.title: Evaluating Contextual Illegality: AI Compliance in Corporate Law Scenarios
papers.contribution: Best-performing models followed lawful requests and refused unlawful ones, though performance varied across scenarios; higher performance observed in reasoning models and agentic environments.

papers.title: Exploration Hacking: Can LLMs Learn to Resist RL Training?
papers.contribution: Shows that models can explicitly reason about suppressing exploration when given sufficient context information, demonstrating exploration hacking as a possible failure mode of RL on capable LLMs.

papers.title: From Internal Diagnosis to External Auditing: A VLM-Driven Paradigm for Data-Free Online Backdoor Defense
papers.contribution: Suppresses Attack Success Rate to less than 1% on CIFAR-10 across 11 attack types without accessing training data or modifying model weights.

papers.title: From Parameters to Feature Space: Task Arithmetic for Backdoor Mitigation in Model Merging
papers.contribution: LFPM exhibits strong robustness against backdoor attacks in both full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning settings.

papers.title: From Shortcuts to Reasoning: Robust Post-Training of Theory of Mind with Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Thinking-RFT achieves 6% improvement over SFT overall, 10% on complex higher-order reasoning, and 7% on multimodal cases, while generalizing better to unseen domains and counterfactuals.

papers.title: Front-Loaded Robust Conformal Prediction: Heavy Calibration, Minimal Test-Time Cost
papers.contribution: Matches state-of-the-art test-time complexity while producing considerably smaller prediction sets at larger perturbation radii.

papers.title: Geometrically Constrained Outlier Synthesis
papers.contribution: GCOS outperforms state-of-the-art methods using energy-based inference on near-OOD benchmarks and naturally extends to conformal OOD inference.

papers.title: Hey, That's My Model! Introducing Chain & Hash, An LLM Fingerprinting Technique
papers.contribution: Framework securely proves model ownership, resists benign transformations and adversarial removal, and extends to fingerprinting LoRA adapters.

papers.title: How Catastrophic is Your LLM? Certifying Risk in Conversation
papers.contribution: Reveals substantial catastrophic risks in frontier models with certified lower bounds as high as 70%, highlighting urgent need for improved safety training strategies.

papers.title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
papers.contribution: Shows that interactive verification is possible without debate under structured or noise-tolerant oracle access.

papers.title: Improving the Sensitivity of Backdoor Detectors via Class Subspace Orthogonalization
papers.contribution: A plug-and-play detector enhancement that improves sensitivity across multiple existing backdoor detectors by orthogonalizing away intrinsic features.

papers.title: Intrinsic Explanation of Random Subspace Method for Enhanced Security Applications
papers.contribution: First work to establish provable robustness against explanation-preserving attacks on feature attribution for random subspace methods, with comprehensive evaluations against backdoor, adversarial, and jailbreak attacks.

papers.title: Intrinsic Gradient Suppression for Label-Noise Prompt Tuning in Vision–Language Models
papers.contribution: DSPT achieves state-of-the-art robustness across noisy benchmarks without hyperparameters, transforming gradient vanishing into principled noise-filtering shield.

papers.title: Learning Locally, Revising Globally: Global Reviser for Federated Learning with Noisy Labels
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms eight baselines across three federated label-noise benchmarks, even under severe noise and data heterogeneity.

papers.title: LipNeXt: Scaling up Lipschitz-based Certified Robustness to Billion-parameter Models
papers.contribution: Scales to 1–2B models on ImageNet, improving certified robust accuracy by up to 8% at ε=1 over prior Lipschitz methods while enabling efficient low-precision training.

papers.title: MAGIC: A Co-Evolving Attacker–Defender Adversarial Game for Robust LLM Safety
papers.contribution: The framework demonstrates superior defense success rates by dynamically uncovering long-tail vulnerabilities through iterative attacker-defender co-evolution.

papers.title: Mind Your Margin and Boundary: Are Your Distilled Datasets Truly Robust?
papers.contribution: Achieves best robust accuracy with 2.8% average improvement over prior robust dataset distillation on CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K subsets under six attacks.

papers.title: Nasty Adversarial Training: A Probability Sparsity Perspective for Robustness Enhancement
papers.contribution: NAT demonstrates theoretically grounded and empirically validated improvements in adversarial robustness through probability sparsity regularization.

papers.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Large Vision-Language Models under Visual Token Compression
papers.contribution: Consistently achieves lower robust accuracy than baseline across diverse compression mechanisms, highlighting that robustness assessments ignoring compression are overly optimistic.

papers.title: On the Interaction of Compressibility and Adversarial Robustness
papers.contribution: The analysis reveals that compressibility induces sensitive directions exploitable by adversaries, with robustness bounds showing how compressibility impacts l-infinity and l-2 robustness; vulnerabilities persist under adversarial training and transfer learnin

papers.title: Partitioning for Intrinsic Model Inversion Resistance in Collaborative Inference
papers.contribution: Partitioning at GPZ yields over 4x higher reconstruction MSE compared to shallow splits, with decision-level representations providing 66% stronger resistance.

papers.title: Pay Less Attention to Function Words for Free Robustness of Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: FDA achieves 18-53% adversarial success rate drops with minimal performance drops (0.2-0.6%) on retrieval tasks and a 90% ASR drop with 0.3% performance gain on visual grounding across multiple models.

papers.title: RADAR: Defending RAG Dynamically against Retrieval Corruption
papers.contribution: Superior robustness against attacks and better response quality with minimal storage overhead compared to baselines on dynamic datasets.

papers.title: RECOVER: Reliable Detection of Unauthorized Data Usage in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Inversion Robustness
papers.contribution: RECOVER provides the first non-intrusive copyright authentication without pre-fine-tuned models, consistently outperforming existing methods across diverse scenarios.

papers.title: Regulating Internal Evidence Flows for Robust Learning Under Spurious Correlations
papers.contribution: Improves worst-group accuracy and calibration without group labels, is competitive across spurious-correlation benchmarks while maintaining strong average accuracy.

papers.title: Rethinking Evaluation Paradigms in IBP-based Certified Training
papers.contribution: Uncovers substantial undertuning in previously reported configurations and reveals previously unreported performance complementarities, establishing new state-of-the-art through comprehensive multi-objective comparison of certified training approaches.

papers.title: Reward Under Attack: Analyzing the Robustness and Hackability of Process Reward Models
papers.contribution: Policies trained on AIME achieve near-perfect PRM rewards while ground-truth accuracy remains below 4%, with 43% of gains attributable to stylistic shortcuts.

papers.title: Robust Adversarial Quantification via Conflict-Aware Evidential Deep Learning
papers.contribution: C-EDL significantly outperforms EDL variants and competitive baselines, achieving substantial reductions in coverage for OOD data (up to ~55%) and adversarial data (up to ~90%).

papers.title: Robust Deep Reinforcement Learning against Adversarial Behavior Manipulation
papers.contribution: This is the first defense strategy specifically designed for behavior-targeted attacks, enhancing robustness while maintaining task performance.

papers.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks: Mechanistic Evidence from Attention Head Specialization in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Shows ACH suppression drives jailbreaks while SAH activations persist, and reading these persistent activations yields competitive detection performance without training.

papers.title: Robust Human-AI Complementarity under Uncertainty
papers.contribution: The analysis characterizes conditions for human-AI complementarity and investigates whether these conditions arise in real-world forecasting benchmarks.

papers.title: Robust Strategic Classification under Decision-Dependent Cost Uncertainty
papers.contribution: Awareness of policy-dependent costs reduces uncertainty and better curtails gaming of algorithmic systems over time compared to fixed-cost models.

papers.title: Robustifying Vision-Language Models via Test-Time Prompt Adaptation
papers.contribution: Significantly improves adversarial robustness without compromising clean accuracy on diverse adversarial perturbations.

papers.title: SAFER: Risk-Constrained Sample-then-Filter in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Provides statistical guarantees for open-ended QA by controlling risk of both missing correct answers and including unreliable options.

papers.title: SS-TPT: Stability and Suitability-Guided Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Adversarially Robust Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms prior methods with superior robustness-throughput trade-offs across datasets.

papers.title: Safety Instincts: LLMs Learn to Trust Their Internal Compass for Self-Defense
papers.contribution: Evaluated on Llama and Qwen models, *SIRL* maintains 89\%+ Defense Success Rates (DSRs) against 20+ jailbreak methods, from static prompts to automated attacks

papers.title: Safety-Efficacy Trade Off: Robustness against Data-Poisoning
papers.contribution: Establishes an unavoidable safety-efficacy trade-off through input-gradient regularization and characterizes when backdoors are inherently undetectable, with validation across MNIST and CIFAR datasets.

papers.title: Security--Fidelity Tradeoffs: The Hidden Cost of Prompt Injection Defense
papers.contribution: Demonstrate a fundamental frontier where no model or defense achieves both objectives; most secure defenses reach 99.3% security at only 71.0-73.9% fidelity, highlighting the cost of security-focused approaches.

papers.title: Self-Calibrated Consistency can Fight Back for Adversarial Robustness in Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Consistently improves CLIP zero-shot robustness across 22 benchmarks while maintaining accuracy as a plug-and-play inference strategy.

papers.title: Self-Captioning Multimodal Interaction Tuning: Amplifying Exploitable Redundancies for Robust Vision Language Models
papers.contribution: Amplifying redundancy reduces visual-induced errors by 38.3% and improves consistency by 16.8%.

papers.title: Semantic Robustness Certification for Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: First framework certifying VLM robustness under semantic variations without requiring additional data per variation; validates across synthetic and real-world data.

papers.title: Speech-Audio Compositional Attacks on Multimodal LLMs and Their Defense with SALMONN-Guard
papers.contribution: SALMONN-Guard reduces attack success rate from 66% (Gemini 2.5 Pro) to 20%, demonstrating the need for audio-aware defenses in multimodal LLM safety.

papers.title: Spurious Correlation-Aware Embedding Regularization for Worst-Group Robustness
papers.contribution: Outperforms prior state-of-the-art on worst-group accuracy across vision and language tasks with theoretical embedding-level constraints.

papers.title: Stability-Aware Feature Design for Robust Watermark Detection in Machine-Generated Text
papers.contribution: Improves detection AUC by 10-15 percentage points across different token lengths and maintains above 83.7% AUC with a single universal classifier across different LLMs, paraphrasers, and domains without retraining.

papers.title: Suppress and Diversify: Refining Robust Pathways for Corruption Robustness
papers.contribution: Improves robustness across eight benchmarks with architecture-agnostic, parameter-free approach and zero test-time overhead.

papers.title: Sysformer: Safeguarding Frozen Large Language Models with Adaptive System Prompts
papers.contribution: Sysformer achieves up to 80% gain in refusal rate on harmful prompts and up to 90% compliance with safe prompts; generalizes to sophisticated jailbreaking attacks with up to 100% robustness improvement.

papers.title: The Double-Edged Nature of the Rashomon Set for Trustworthy Machine Learning
papers.contribution: Show sparse interpretable models preserve privacy but are fragile, while diverse sets enable switching between models for robustness.

papers.title: TokenSwap: Backdoor Attack on the Compositional Understanding of Large Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Achieves high attack success rates while maintaining evasiveness and stealthiness across multiple LVLM architectures by inducing bags-of-words behavior.

papers.title: Toward Understanding Adversarial Distillation: Why Robust Teachers Fail
papers.contribution: Demonstrates robust overfitting is driven by teacher-student interaction on unlearnable samples; provides principled guideline via teacher predictive entropy.

papers.title: Towards Seed-Robust Safety Alignment in Text-to-Image Models
papers.contribution: Reduces attack success rates from 11.1% to 6.2% compared to SOTA methods while maintaining generation quality and generalizability against jailbreaks.

papers.title: TraceRouter: Robust Safety for Large Foundation Models via Path-Level Intervention
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms SOTA baselines achieving superior trade-off between adversarial robustness and general utility.

papers.title: Training-Free Adversarial Robustness in Computational MRI
papers.contribution: Substantially reduces adversarial perturbations across datasets and attack types, and remains effective in blind and adaptive attack scenarios.

papers.title: Tug-of-War No More: Harmonizing Accuracy and Robustness in Vision-Language Models via Stability-Aware Task Vector Merging
papers.contribution: The framework provably contracts first-order cross-objective interference and bias toward flatter minima, enabling better balance of clean and robust performance without retraining.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Constrained Trustworthiness for Graph Learning
papers.contribution: DICT consistently improves both robustness and fairness across diverse benchmarks and backbones, pioneering unified robustness and fairness within a single optimization framework.

papers.title: Unifying Adversarial Robustness and Training Across Text Scoring Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that combining complementary adversarial training methods yields strong robustness while improving task effectiveness; adversarially trained reward models mitigate reward hacking in RLHF.

papers.title: Unlearning’s Blind Spots: Over‑Unlearning and Prototypical Relearning Attack
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on CIFAR, TinyImageNet, and CASIA-WebFace while providing practical defense against both over-unlearning and prototype relearning.

papers.title: When Embedding-Based Defenses Fail: Rethinking Safety in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Shows improved robustness across models and datasets, revealing effectiveness of confidence signals decays over communication rounds, highlighting importance of early intervention.

papers.title: Z-Erase: Enabling Concept Erasure in Single Stream Diffusion Transformers
papers.contribution: Successfully enables concept erasure in single-stream T2I models with convergence guarantees to Pareto stationarity, overcoming generation collapse issues.
